opportunities.fit_rationale: Lab does technical research rather than pure capacity-building or discourse, though university research inherently supports students.

opportunities.summary: Cloudflare credits for startups, varying by the amount raised.
opportunities.amount_quote: Tier 3: $10,000 under $1M raised. Tier 2: $100,000 under $5M raised. Tier 1: $350,000 at $5M or more raised.
opportunities.eligibility_reason: Tiers are based on startup funding raised, which academic labs don't have.
opportunities.fit_rationale: Provides infrastructure credits, but the lab is an academic entity, not a funded startup.

opportunities.summary: Swiss nonprofit focused on reducing suffering risks, including that posed by catastrophic AI misuse and AI conflict. Makes both grants to nonprofits and investments in for-profit companies.
opportunities.eligibility_quote: grants to nonprofits and investments in for-profit companies.
opportunities.eligibility_reason: Lab is academic (university), which functions broadly as a nonprofit, but the specific suffering risks focus is a stretch.
opportunities.fit_rationale: The focus is explicitly on 'reducing suffering risks,' which is only tangentially related to the lab's general scientific autonomous agent research.

opportunities.summary: Funding to facilitate the development of AI-powered cybersecurity capabilities for defenders through grants, API credits, and other support.
opportunities.deadline_quote: OpenAI will evaluate and accept applications for funding or other support on a rolling basis.
opportunities.amount_quote: We will grant in increments of $10,000 USD from a fund of $1M USD, in the form of API credits, direct funding and/or equivalents.
opportunities.eligibility_quote: If you share our vision for a secure and innovative AI-driven future, we invite you to submit your proposals and join us in our aim towards enhancing defensive cybersecurity technologies.
opportunities.eligibility_reason: There are no stated geographic or institutional restrictions, and academic researchers are eligible to apply provided the project focuses on defensive cybersecurity.
opportunities.fit_rationale: The lab's focus is primarily on autonomous AI research agents and automated machine learning rather than cybersecurity, though some elements of its work on AI safety, agent governance, and audits could potentially align with defensive cybersecurity agents.

results.program: Manufacturing, Trade & Connectivity Young Individual Research Grant (MTC YIRG)
results.funder: Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR)
results.summary: Supports Singapore-based, early-career researchers for independent, curiosity-driven research in physical sciences and engineering areas.
results.deadline_quote: closes on 23 June 2026, 11:59 pm (Singapore Standard Time).
results.amount_quote: Funding of up to S$325,000 per project (inclusive of 30% indirect costs) is available for a project duration of up to three years.
results.eligibility_reason: The applicant is faculty at a local publicly funded institute (SMU), which meets the employment criteria, but it is unspecified if they received their PhD within the 7-year limit.
results.fit_rationale: The lab's research on computational AI and autonomous agents falls well within engineering areas. However, funding is contingent on the applicant being an early-career researcher and meeting institutional quotas.

results.quote: The list of projects awarded under the MTC YIRG Grant Call can be found here.

awaiting_results.program: Middle Powers and Transformative AI Request for Proposals
awaiting_results.summary: Funding for researchers, writers, builders and conveners on how middle powers can stay relevant in and help safeguard the AI transition through research, strategy, policy engagement, and building institutions.
awaiting_results.eligibility_quote: Individuals, informal teams, universities, fiscally-sponsored organizations and non-profits (including non-profit projects within for-profit organizations) are all among the groups who are able to apply.
awaiting_results.eligibility_reason: The applicant is a faculty member at a university in Singapore, which fits both the eligible organization types and the list of permitted jurisdictions.
awaiting_results.fit_rationale: The lab's research on AI safety, accountability, governance of autonomous agents, and verification technology directly aligns with the RFP's interest in independent evaluation and verification. Furthermore, the applicant is based in Singapore, a key middle power explicitly highlighted in the call.

awaiting_results.summary: This grant funds global teams to develop advanced AI agents that work with human researchers to generate and test new cancer research hypotheses, transforming how cancer is studied.
awaiting_results.eligibility_reason: The applicant operates a global academic research lab.
awaiting_results.fit_rationale: The methodology exactly mirrors the lab's goal of AI agents collaborating with humans for scientific discovery (generating/testing hypotheses). It would require applying this computational pipeline to cancer research.

awaiting_results.program: Anthropic Fellows Program for AI Safety Research
awaiting_results.summary: Anthropic Fellows Program for AI Safety Research supports engineers and researchers with mentorship and resources for empirical AI safety and security work aimed at public research outputs.
awaiting_results.eligibility_reason: The applicant is an academic researcher.
awaiting_results.fit_rationale: The lab studies empirical AI safety, including evaluation methodology, robust learning, and verifiable outcomes, tightly aligning with empirical AI safety and security work.

awaiting_results.program: Iliad Fellowships in Applied Mathematics for AI Safety
awaiting_results.summary: This fellowship supports individuals passionate about mathematics and building safer AI systems, focusing on theory-driven research on ReLU networks and projects that raise the epistemic bar of AI safety.
awaiting_results.amount: Up to $6,000 per month travel-and-housing allowance
awaiting_results.amount_quote: Up to $6,000 per month travel-and-housing allowance for the 3-month fellowship
awaiting_results.eligibility_quote: Mathematicians are especially welcome, regardless of prior AI experience.
awaiting_results.eligibility_reason: The call is open to individuals raising the epistemic bar of AI safety, which aligns with the applicant, but implies relocating for 3 months which may be difficult for active faculty.
awaiting_results.fit_rationale: While the focus on raising the epistemic bar of AI safety aligns with the lab's goal of verifiable AI and accountability, the fellowship has a strong mathematics/ReLU network focus and appears geared toward temporary relocation.

changes.after: Up to $6,000 per month travel-and-housing allowance

awaiting_results.program: Sony Research Award Program Focused Research Award
awaiting_results.summary: Collaborative research track providing funding for focused joint research between a university and Sony in areas like AI, Large Language Models, robotics, and computer vision.
awaiting_results.deadline_quote: The 2026 deadline is 15 September 2026 at 11:59pm Pacific
awaiting_results.amount_quote: Up to $150,000 USD per proposal (1 year, renewable)
awaiting_results.eligibility_quote: The PI must be a full-time faculty member or researcher at a recognized institution - Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, Professor or equivalent researcher - and must be able to supervise PhD students.
awaiting_results.eligibility_reason: The applicant is a faculty member at a recognized university institution.
awaiting_results.fit_rationale: The lab's research closely matches Sony's interests in AI and Large Language Models, fitting the call for joint research and industry awards in AI.

awaiting_results.summary: Funding for career development, transitions, independent study, graduate study, and internships for individuals seeking to reduce global catastrophic risks or improve the long-term future, particularly in AI safety and biosecurity.
awaiting_results.deadline_quote: We’ll also continue to process all applications submitted on or before September 4.
awaiting_results.eligibility_quote: open to receiving applications from individuals who are already pursuing careers related to reducing global catastrophic risk (or otherwise improving the long-term future), looking to transition into such careers from other lines of work, or only just starting their careers. ... The program is open to applicants in any country.
awaiting_results.eligibility_reason: The applicant is a faculty member working on AI safety and governance, which perfectly aligns with the focus. The program explicitly supports researchers in any country and lists 'A professor in machine learning... who wants funding to take a one-year sabbatical to explore ways to contribute to technical AI safety' as a concrete example of a fit.
awaiting_results.fit_rationale: The lab's research includes AI safety and governance of autonomous agents, directly supporting the program's goal to mitigate risks from advanced AI. As an academic, the applicant can use this funding for independent study or a sabbatical.

awaiting_results.summary: An eight-week, fully remote fellowship offering financial support, compute credits, and API credits to conduct research in AI safety and alignment.
awaiting_results.eligibility_quote: The fellowship is intended for people who are interested in AI safety and alignment research and can demonstrate the ability to think carefully about challenging technical or conceptual problems.
awaiting_results.eligibility_reason: The applicant researches AI safety and governance of autonomous agents, meeting the interest requirement, and the fully remote format accommodates their location in Singapore.
awaiting_results.fit_rationale: The fellowship perfectly matches the lab's stated research directions in AI safety, and specifically provides the LLM API credits and cloud/GPU compute the lab needs.

awaiting_results.summary: An 8-week paid research fellowship for AI alignment researchers to work on projects defined by AIAF, experiencing an agile methodology to accelerate research.
awaiting_results.deadline_quote: Applications for the 2026 cohort closed on August 17, 2026 (AoE).
awaiting_results.amount_quote: The $12,000 stipend is paid in 2 installments over the duration of the program.
awaiting_results.eligibility_quote: Any career stage: recent PhDs, MSc students, self-taught researchers, or people transitioning into AI alignment from another field.
awaiting_results.eligibility_reason: The applicant is a faculty member with an ML background, and the fellowship is fully remote and open to individuals from any country and at any career stage.
awaiting_results.fit_rationale: The lab's focus on AI safety and governance aligns with the fellowship's focus on AI alignment. However, the fellowship requires substantially all of your working time for 8 weeks, which may be difficult for a full-time faculty member to commit to.
